findings.evidence: “Once the body is written, create or update the PR as phase 5 specifies, passing the title from `$AD/title.txt` in the same call” repeats phase 5's title-file requirement; final-message ordering is likewise restated in phases 2 and 6.
findings.fix: Keep each invariant's complete wording at its owning phase and use short cross-references elsewhere. Record the consolidation in docs/audit/recovery/explain-pr-changes/record.md without dropping any distinct requirement or attribution.

findings.evidence: The command is 388 lines. Templates and recovery recipes are already split into skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, but the command still embeds lengthy state-persistence and failure-message procedures throughout phases 2–6.
findings.fix: Move the detailed shell-state bootstrap and repeated failure-message recipes into a dedicated section of skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, explicitly loaded when executing the phased workflow. Keep phase ordering, safety gates and routing in the command, and record the moves.

findings.evidence: “Append `MODE` to `$AD/state.env` (`printf 'MODE=%q\n'`).” The shown printf supplies no value; Bash therefore formats an empty string, so following it persists an empty MODE rather than the selected attach or branch mode.
findings.fix: Show the complete persistence command: `printf 'MODE=%q\n' "$MODE" >> "$AD/state.env"`. Check that sourcing state.env in the next Bash call restores the selected mode.

findings.evidence: The required none-mode filter matches `!\[[^]]*\](\[[^]]*\])?` without excluding inline images. With `[logo]: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/example` and `![logo](https://static.example.com/logo.png)`, its final awk pass removes `![logo]` because the label is in att, corrupting an ordinary-host image that section 1.3 requires preserving.
findings.fix: Make the reference-image pass distinguish inline images followed by `(` from reference-style or shortcut images, preserving inline images untouched after the inline-image filter. Verify this mixed-definition case preserves the complete ordinary-host image while removing actual diagram references.
